reason: This text (1 Samuel 14) demonstrates substantial agency exercised by non-leaders. The armor-bearer (נושא כליו), a subordinate soldier, makes critical decisions: he chooses to accompany Jonathan, declares his willingness to follow him ('עֲשֵׂ֖ה כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ'), and participates actively in combat. The common people (הָעָם) also exercise agency by independently pursuing the Philistines, violating Saul's oath by eating food, bringing their own livestock for slaughter, and ultimately defending Jonathan's life against Saul's death sentence ('חָלִ֗ילָה... חַי־ יְהוָה'). Jonathan himself, though of royal blood, is not the formal leader (Saul is) yet initiates and controls the military action. The narrative demonstrates that consequential decisions and meaningful actions are taken across multiple hierarchical levels, not exclusively by formal leaders.
